findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. On the first screen they can already say what it is and why it matters.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: This page is the site's front page, but the title and almost all of the body are about another project, firstmate, which the newcomer has probably never heard of. The page also never shows Athena's main output, a commit tied to the request, the models, the cost and the verdict, so the demonstration does not match the pitch.
findings.source: Title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" and lede "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project"

findings.text: The next step is easy to find from the top. It gives prerequisites, a clone command, ./setup.sh and a sample `athena ask "add a changelog"`, so a newcomer knows what to do. It does not say which operating systems are supported, or whether Rust or a paid Claude account is needed.
findings.source: header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the Next steps section

findings.text: This link sits right in the opening material but is meant for the repository owner. A newcomer can't tell whether it applies to them, and it pulls attention away from the install link.
findings.source: header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The study does try to bring a stranger in. It has a plain one-line definition of firstmate, terms defined before use, and a step-by-step walk through one task. The terms "ship" and "local-only ship" are used here before they are defined.
findings.source: Heading "Start here" and its "Words used first" list

findings.text: The body moves quickly into state-machine detail: transition ids, exit codes and pending-close records. A newcomer who wanted to judge Athena will probably skim it, not learn from it.
findings.source: Headings "Transitions" and "Counters": "places-held, changed by transitions t1, t3, t4, t9, t11"; card t2 "exits 75"

findings.text: Some sentences use Athena's internal words ("job", "recorded boundary", "studies/") without saying which repository or idea they mean, so a stranger can't follow them.
findings.source: Heading "Limits of this study": "The job gave no recorded boundary for running firstmate"; "About this page": "the name of the folder under studies/"

findings.text: Every statement can be traced to exact lines in firstmate's source. This is concrete proof of the page's opening promise of traceable, accountable output.
findings.source: Heading "Claims and sources": each claim links to a file and line range at the pinned commit
